newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Bankers to propose world self-regulation standards.
newsitem.headline: Bankers to propose world self-regulation standards.

text.p: Leading commerial bankers have called for a set of global standards -- a form of self-regulation -- to cover financial institutions that are active internationally.

John Heimann, chairman global financial institutions at Merrill Lynch & Co, told a briefing at the International Monetary Conference (IMF) that a report to be issued by the Group of Thirty leading banks shortly would recommend a private sector initiative to set standards in close cooperation with various national supervisors.
"There is an inherent contradiction in national supervision of global firms and global markets that limit the financial system's defenses against systemic disruption," Heimann said.
The initiative envisons the creation of a steering committee that would group major financial institutions and regulators.

This committee would look at the issues of risk management policies, centralisation of activities regardless of legal structure and articulate standards for institutions' board of directors, their management and external auditors.

Financial industry supervisors currently face three key problems. Financial instruments are increasingly complex, differences between banks and non-banks are blurring and institutions operate globally. However, supervision is essentially limited to national boundaries.
Although banking supervisors cooperate in the Basle Committee on Banking Supervision to set international standards, the legal framework for these standards is purely national.
Supervisors from the bank, insurance and securities industries are also cooperating in the Joint Forum to try to improve their understanding of how to regulate financial conglomerates.

"What is clearly required is a better system for evaluating the risk management and internal controls of global firms on a cross-border and cross-functional basis, both in the market place and among regulators," Heimann said.
